# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been checked out forty-one times. Marion found it while flipping through the pages at the returns desk, checking for damage the way she'd done every morning for nineteen years. On page 248, beside a sentence about Heathcliff's departure, someone had written in careful pencil: *He leaves at night, not dawn. See Ch. 3.*

Marion frowned. The pencil marks were small, precise, the letters formed with the neatness of someone who'd learned cursive when it was still taught properly. She checked the checkout card—old habits; the system had been digital for a decade, but she still printed the due dates on paper slips tucked in the back. The last borrower was listed only as *Hobbs, R.*

She erased the note. That was policy. Pencil marks, dog-ears, coffee rings—erase, flatten, wipe. But her eraser hovered a moment longer than usual, because the correction was *right*. She checked Chapter 3. Heathcliff did leave at night.
